title: Cap 2'-O-methyltransferase CMTR2 regulates male meiosis independent of its methyltransferase activity.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Opened the Zenodo deposit via its application programming interface: it is one 51,531-byte zip of analysis code (CC-BY-4.0), no data. Listed the GitHub repository ycli1995/scRNAseq20250919 through the GitHub API: 28 entries, all R and Python plotting/clustering scripts, largest 152 KB, zero data files. Tried the Genome Sequence Archive (GSA) page for CRA030115 three ways (helper fetch, browser-style request, download mirror): blocked by a JavaScript bot check or 404, so I could not list the deposited files. Europe PMC supplementary-file endpoint timed out twice, so supplementary tables were not retrievable.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the only deposited dataset is raw single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) reads for control and Ddx4-GcKO (germ-cell knockout) testes at postnatal day 12; that 69,362 cells passed quality control at a median of 3,620 unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) and 1,992 genes per cell; that libraries were made with the Singleron GEXSCOPE kit and processed by 'a customized bioinformatics pipeline'; and all wet-lab measurements (quantitative PCR, immunoblot, cross-linking immunoprecipitation, luciferase, messenger RNA half-lives) which are reported only as figures at n = 3.

a1_downloadable.note: GSA accession CRA030115 is a public deposit needing no access application, so A1 is not a formal failure, but I could not list or download a single file: the GSA web interface requires JavaScript execution and the download mirror returned 404. The only thing that actually downloaded was 51 KB of code from Zenodo.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAILS. There is no feature/label table anywhere. Any target one might model here - cell type, genotype, messenger RNA (mRNA) stability, pseudotime stage - would have to be constructed from raw sequencing reads by re-running the authors' unreleased custom pipeline. No processed count matrix, no differential-expression table and no half-life table were deposited in GSA, Zenodo or GitHub.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAILS. Inputs are raw FASTQ reads only. The gene-by-cell expression matrix that every downstream analysis used was never deposited, and the Singleron GEXSCOPE barcode chemistry means standard CellRanger cannot be used; the paper calls the read processing 'a customized bioinformatics pipeline' without releasing it.

a4_units_stated.note: Not the blocker: UMI (unique molecular identifier) counts and the quality-control thresholds (>71,000 UMIs, >20% mitochondrial, <240 or >8,500 genes) are stated in the methods. Verified in the paper text, not in files.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAILS at the level of the independent unit. 69,362 cells sounds large, but they come from one control and one knockout mouse at a single age, so the genotype comparison has n = 1 per group and cells are not independent replicates. All other measurements in the paper are n = 3 wells of quantitative PCR or immunoblot, read off figures.

a6_fits_laptop.note: FAILS. Raw 150 bp paired-end NovaSeq scRNA-seq FASTQ for ~69,000 cells is tens to hundreds of gigabytes (size not verifiable because the GSA listing was blocked), exceeds the project's 50 MB download cap, is explicitly excluded as raw sequencing data, and alignment would need far more than a 16 GB CPU-only laptop.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked at all - no data file was retrievable, so the 69,362-cell and 12-cluster claims are unverifiable against anything.

a8_label_provenance.note: The nearest thing to a label is the cell-type annotation, which is a human assignment made on top of Seurat clustering of the same expression matrix that would be the features - a label computed from the features, which is the leakage-by-construction case A8 is written to catch. The pseudotime ordering is likewise an algorithm output, not a measurement.

existing_models.name: UTR-Insight (deep model for 5' untranslated region function, from search results only)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search snippet reports it explains 89.1% of mean ribosome load variation on random 5' untranslated regions and 82.8% on endogenous ones; I read the snippet, not the paper, so treat the number as unverified.

existing_models.name: RNAdegformer (nucleotide-resolution messenger RNA degradation predictor, Briefings in Bioinformatics 2023, from search results only)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved beyond the title and abstract snippet.

backbone.name: RNA-FM or a 5' untranslated region language model would be the natural fit for the sequence-to-stability task, and scGPT/Geneformer for the single-cell task
backbone.hardware: Irrelevant here: no input table exists to embed.

integration.partner_dataset: None usable. In principle the mouse testis single-cell atlases (e.g. the published five-strain mouse testis resource) would join on gene symbol plus cell type, but this paper contributes no processed matrix to join with.
integration.join_key: gene symbol / Ensembl gene (would be available only after building the matrix ourselves)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written usefully, because the join would need a count matrix this paper never released.

controls.positive_control: Would have been recovering canonical testis marker genes per cell type (e.g. Ddx4 in germ cells, Sox9 in Sertoli cells) - but not runnable without the matrix.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling would be runnable in principle; moot without data.
controls.external_validation: Public mouse testis single-cell atlases exist and would serve as external validation, which is the one genuinely attractive feature of this topic.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim is available: with one control and one knockout mouse and no released expression matrix, any model here would describe two animals' cells processed by a pipeline nobody else can reproduce.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use single-cell gene expression from mouse testis to predict which germ cells are arrested in meiosis after a gene is deleted.
plain_idea.train_on: Would have been the gene-by-cell expression matrix for testis cells from control and germ-cell knockout mice; the paper reports 69,362 cells after quality control, but no matrix was deposited, so the usable count is zero.
plain_idea.predict: Would have been the cell's developmental stage (undifferentiated spermatogonia through zygotene spermatocyte) or its genotype; the 'true answer' is a human annotation of computational clusters, not an independent measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Reproductive-biology labs would like an automatic stage caller that flags where a knockout arrests, which is now done by eye; but this paper supplies no data to build or test one.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: an automatic spermatogenic-stage classifier, or a 5' untranslated region sequence model of messenger RNA stability trained on CMTR2-dependent transcripts. The first dies because no processed single-cell matrix exists and the stage label is itself derived from the features; the second dies because the paper measures half-lives for exactly two transcripts (Spdya and Mov10l1) in figure panels at n = 3.

effort.compute_note: No estimate possible: the GSA file listing was unreachable, so raw read volume is unknown, and rebuilding a count matrix from Singleron GEXSCOPE FASTQ with an unreleased custom pipeline has no defensible time or memory estimate. Nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Ask whether a processed count matrix exists anywhere - it does not. Zenodo holds 51 KB of R/Python scripts, GitHub holds 28 script files and no data, and the sole data deposit is raw FASTQ. That check took two tool calls and killed the project.

verdict_reason: Only raw sequencing reads were deposited; no processed matrix, no label column, and the genotype comparison rests on one mouse per group.
